Named decision: `machine-clause-delimiters`, confirmed 2026-10-30.

Machine header clauses have no trailing semicolons. This applies uniformly to
`requires`, `ensures`, `reaches`, `invokes`, `suspends`, `blocks`, `crashes`,
`terminates` (including `terminates by`), and other machine header clauses.
The next clause keyword or the implementation body delimits a clause; a newline
does not change its owner. A checked machine proceeds directly from its last
clause to its body. A semicolon before that body does not terminate a clause and
then resume the same declaration.

A bodyless machine declaration or requirement ends with one semicolon after its
complete header. That terminator belongs to the declaration, not whichever
clause happens to come last. A nested `requires machine` is such a declaration:
its semicolon closes the nested contract and subsequent clauses belong to the
enclosing declaration.

```omega
machine invoke<machine Step>() -> u64
requires machine Step() -> u64
    terminates;
crashes Trap
{
    Step()
}
```

Here `terminates` belongs to `Step`, and `crashes Trap` belongs to `invoke`.
To put a crash ceiling on `Step`, put that clause before its declaration
terminator. A callback with several operational axes writes them together:

```omega
requires machine Target() -> u64
    suspends
    blocks
    terminates;
```

No extra semicolon is needed after a termination clause to end that callable.
An additional same-level terminator rejects; it is not a compatibility spelling.
[Nested callable families](generics.md#nested-contracts-and-proof-families) still
have one terminator per bodyless declaration: closing an inner requirement and
then its enclosing bodyless requirement legitimately needs two declaration
terminators. Neither is a clause terminator. Statement, data-field, and other
declaration punctuation is unchanged by this rule.

Machine `requires` applies at every invocation, including terminal and recursive
calls. Every arrival establishes the target's requirements and declared domains
under actual argument substitution. Nesting does not assume the parent's entry
requirements again, import its return guarantees, or supply facts invalidated
by mutation. Live caller facts can discharge a nested helper's requirements;
body inference must justify any inferred private requirements on every arrival,
not grant them from lexical ancestry. Every invocation retains both sides of
its own contract. A recursive contract is not its own proof; induction follows
the well-founded obligations in [termination](termination.md).

Arrival substitution is simultaneous and identity-based. Scalar arguments retain
their evaluation snapshots; facts about referenced storage must survive writes
from later arguments. A same-named formal cannot alias an unrelated caller value.
Every reachable predecessor participates in a join. Unknown input cannot be
omitted to preserve a convenient invariant. A minimum collection length is not
an exact extent, and declaration initializers are not recurring loop invariants.

Facts apply to their exact subjects and program points. Assignments first
[capture their destination place](expressions.md#evaluation-schedule), including
its selectors and bounds at that program point. They then evaluate the
right-hand side and its effects, capture transferable evidence, and finally
invalidate overlapping destination facts and establish the new value at the
captured place. Right-hand-side mutations invalidate their own overlapping facts
when they occur; the captured selector is not a fact that the selector's live
binding still has its earlier value. Uninitialized storage
has no assumed zero. Copies transport facts about the captured value, not source
expressions to be reevaluated after mutation.

Declared measures are package-private; `public measure` rejects, and other packages
cannot name them directly. An exported machine may use its package's private
measure because callers depend on the promise, not the witness. Cross-package
operational recursion remains unsupported pending a compositional termination
interface that closes from published evidence without inspecting private measures.

`terminates by subject -> View` selects a well-founded ranking theory. The view
may be descending naturals, an increasing value approaching a fixed bound,
proper subtree, or a lexicographic product. An unbounded increasing view is not
well-founded. Authors need not synthesize subtraction to express a bounded
increasing cursor; the view owns normalization.

An optional `in lower..=upper` constrains the rank produced by the view, not
storage capacity. Its lower bound establishes the floor. Short form without
`-> View` requires a carrier-declared stable canonical default, immediately
elaborated to an explicit view. A uniquely visible user measure is not a default;
adding another declaration cannot reinterpret existing code.

Terminating recursive machines use one joint ranking for the entire strongly
connected call component, whether declarations are nested or top-level and
whether an edge is an ordinary call or terminal transfer. Edges may preserve
rank only if every complete cycle contains strict descent. A DFS-selected
subset of cycles is insufficient. There is no separate source-state ranking
rule; lexical containment is not a recursion or induction boundary.
The exact source spelling for differently shaped mutual participants remains
undetermined; the joint-cycle semantic rule is settled.

One component cites its relation and well-foundedness evidence once, with a
comparison proof for every internal edge and a global every-cycle descent check.
Local decreases cannot prove well-foundedness. An admitted custom ranking theory
makes dependent recursive proofs admission-dependent. Calls outside the component
use ordinary contract application. [Terminal control](../terminal-psi/control_flow.md)
defines reconstruction and grouped certificates.

Computed next subjects use ordinary decrease obligations and cited lemmas; strict
syntactic subterms are an automation tier, not the semantic limit. Rank ranges,
argumented-view bounds, subject substitutions, and all comparisons retain exact
normalized witness identity. Checked diagnostics use `terminates by`, not a
retired alternative spelling.

Runtime recursive call cycles are tail-position only and lower to constant-stack
iteration. Ranking proves termination; tail position permits that lowering.
Ranked non-tail recursion is valid in proof/compile-time use and rejects runtime
lowering. After recursive cycles lower to backedges, the runtime call graph is
acyclic for activation-storage planning. This is context-sensitive eligibility
of one machine construct, not a separate proof language.

Machine header clauses have no trailing semicolons. This applies uniformly to
`requires`, `ensures`, `reaches`, `invokes`, `suspends`, `blocks`, `crashes`,
`terminates` (including `terminates by`), and other machine header clauses.
The next clause keyword or the implementation body delimits a clause; a newline
does not change its owner. A checked machine proceeds directly from its last
clause to its body. A semicolon before that body does not terminate a clause and
then resume the same declaration.

A bodyless machine declaration or requirement ends with one semicolon after its
complete header. That terminator belongs to the declaration, not whichever
clause happens to come last. A nested `requires machine` is such a declaration:
its semicolon closes the nested contract and subsequent clauses belong to the
enclosing declaration.

```omega
machine invoke<machine Step>() -> u64
requires machine Step() -> u64
    terminates;
crashes Trap
{
    Step()
}
```

Here `terminates` belongs to `Step`, and `crashes Trap` belongs to `invoke`.
To put a crash ceiling on `Step`, put that clause before its declaration
terminator. A callback with several operational axes writes them together:

```omega
requires machine Target() -> u64
    suspends
    blocks
    terminates;
```

No extra semicolon is needed after a termination clause to end that callable.
An additional same-level terminator rejects; it is not a compatibility spelling.
[Nested callable families](generics.md#nested-contracts-and-proof-families) still
have one terminator per bodyless declaration: closing an inner requirement and
then its enclosing bodyless requirement legitimately needs two declaration
terminators. Neither is a clause terminator. Statement, data-field, and other
declaration punctuation is unchanged by this rule.
